title: Sales/CS feature request consolidation cadence and rapid-prototype scoping
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Create a lightweight, repeatable consolidation cadence and a rapid-prototype scoping template for Sales and Customer Success feature requests that are non-bug, enterprise-focused. This ticket codifies the intake fields, a weekly consolidation cadence, initial scoring heuristics, and a defined handoff artifact that allows PMs and Eng to make fast go/no-go decisions and sequence work into Dedicated/Private product workstreams.

Why this exists: Sales and CS frequently surface enterprise requests that are large in scope or require regulatory considerations. These requests currently arrive as ad-hoc Slack threads, email threads, and CRM notes. Engineering and PM time are wasted re-gathering context. We need a reproducible process that preserves customer nuance but reduces friction for initial scoping so we can prioritize based on product strategy, revenue potential, and technical risk.

Scope of this ticket:
- Define a one-page "consolidation brief" template (fields below) used by SDR/AE/CS to summarize requests for the weekly review.
- Define a 3-question technical feasibility quick-check for Eng leads.
- Define scoring heuristics (value, effort, compliance risk, strategic alignment) and a pass/fail prototype gating rule.
- Define the weekly consolidation cadence (roles, meeting length, expected artifacts).
- Create a rapid-prototype scoping checklist that maps to engineering inputs required for a 2-week spike or proof-of-concept.
- Define handoff artifacts to PM/ENG backlog (required links, acceptance criteria, test scenarios, security flags).

Consolidation brief template fields (one page):
- Customer name and segment (enterprise/mid-market/startup)
- Request title (1 line)
- Problem statement (1-2 sentences describing pain)
- Current workaround and frequency (how they're solving it today and impact)
- Desired outcome and success metrics (customer-stated)
- License / contract info (relevant CLM or ARR estimate)
- Security/compliance flags (data residency, encryption/KMS, audit logs)
- Timeline & buying signals (P0/P1/long-term)
- Suggested initial solution class (API param, model variant, routing policy, new Console UI)
- Supporting artifacts (PRDs, architecture diagrams, emails, demos)

Initial scoring heuristic (numeric, 1-10 each):
- Customer value (revenue/strategic): 1-10
- Implementation effort (approx dev-weeks): mapped to score 1-10
- Compliance/safety risk: 1 (low) - 10 (high)
- Product alignment: 1-10
- Overall priority score = weighted sum (value x0.35, effort x -0.25, compliance x -0.2, alignment x0.3).

Pass/fail prototype gating rule:
- If priority score >= 6.5 -> consider for 2-week rapid-prototype (spike) with Eng lead assigned.
- If compliance score >= 7 -> require security and legal pre-approval before prototype.
- If implementation effort estimated > 12 dev-weeks -> require an EPIC-level business case and sales commitment before scheduling.

Weekly consolidation cadence (30 minutes):
- Attendees: 1x PM owner, 1x Sales rep rotating, 1x CS rep rotating, 1x Eng lead (ops), Solutions Architect (optional).
- Agenda: 5m quick status; 3 briefs (5m each) with scoring pre-filled; 5m decisions and actions.
- Outputs: updated tickets in Linear with consolidation brief attached, decisions: {prototype, backlog, needs-more-info, declined}.

Rapid-prototype scoping checklist (for 2-week spike):
- Clear success criteria and acceptance tests derived from customer success metrics.
- Minimal viable implementation plan (what to change: routing rule, small new endpoint, Console toggle).
- Data/security checklist completed (if customer data involved).
- Engineering spike tasks and deliverables (experiment, integration test plan, performance target).
- Demo plan for Sales/CS and next-step options (configurable release, dedicated capacity estimate, contractual obligations).

Handoff artifact to backlog (required):
- Link to consolidation brief, priority score, prototype decision, eng spike ticket keys, security/legal notes, supporting docs, and customer contact for follow-ups.

Success metrics for this initiative (what we will measure):
- Median time from first sales mention to PM decision (target: <= 10 business days).
- % of requests that have a usable consolidation brief attached at decision time (target: >= 80%).
- Feedback score from Sales/CS on process (target: >= 4/5).

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Sales push for fast delivery without proper security review. Mitigation: mandatory compliance gating and a template field that surfaces legal flags early.
- Risk: Over-indexing on high-revenue but misaligned requests. Mitigation: weight product alignment in scoring and require EPIC-level signoff for long efforts.

Implementation plan (next steps):
- Draft consolidation brief and scoring sheet (owner: Jonah) by 2025-02-18.
- Run two-week pilot cadence with two AE/CS pairs and Eng on-call during 2025-02-24 to 2025-03-07.
- Collect pilot metrics and iterate template and weighting by 2025-03-14.

Stakeholders: PMs (Aisha, Jonah), Sales leadership (Maya Chen), CS leadership (Liam O'Connor), Eng leads (Ravi Desai), Solutions Architecture (Priya Rao), Security (Elena Morales).
